quarterly_data.quarter: Nissan Chemical annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (FY2026): net sales JPY 279,586 million (+JPY 28,221 million, +11.2% YoY), operating profit JPY 63,552 million (+JPY 6,719 million), ordinary profit JPY 65,897 million and net income attributable to owners of the parent JPY 49,707 million; net sales and every profit line beat both the prior year and the company's forecast (net sales JPY 272,200 million, operating profit JPY 59,000 million). Management states semiconductor materials in the Functional Materials segment drove the whole group, lifting operating profit (+12%) and ordinary profit to record highs, while the segments other than Functional Materials together grew operating profit by only about 2%.
quarterly_data.figure: net sales JPY 279,586 million (+11.2%); operating profit JPY 63,552 million; ordinary profit JPY 65,897 million; net income JPY 49,707 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Nissan Chemical annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Functional Materials segment, FY2026 (year ended March 2026): sales JPY 113,377 million (+13.3% YoY) and operating profit JPY 35,331 million, both above the company's forecast. In semiconductor materials, sales of anti-reflective coatings for semiconductors (ARC) and multi-layer materials (OptiStack) rose sharply on customers' strong utilisation; display materials (SUNEVER polyimide for LCD alignment layers) declined; inorganic colloids (SNOWTEX polishing agents for electronic materials and surface treatments, plus oil and gas materials that raise shale oil and gas extraction efficiency) grew. The report notes that ARC and OptiStack are registered trademarks of Brewer Science, Inc.
quarterly_data.figure: Functional Materials sales JPY 113,377 million (+13.3%); operating profit JPY 35,331 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Nissan Chemical annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Other segments, FY2026 (year ended March 2026): Chemicals sales JPY 39,313 million (+3.9%), operating profit JPY 1,107 million, with basic chemicals growth from high-purity sulfuric acid (a cleaning agent for semiconductors) and urea / AdBlue, while ammonia output was below the prior year; Agricultural Chemicals sales JPY 96,243 million (+11.6%), operating profit JPY 26,043 million (fluralaner animal-health active ingredient up, domestic rice herbicides up on higher rice prices, overseas fungicide sales strong); Healthcare sales JPY 5,224 million (-12.8%); Trading (wholesale) sales JPY 128,899 million (+10.0%), operating profit JPY 3,813 million; Others sales JPY 31,755 million (+8.8%).

quarterly_data.quarter: Nissan Chemical annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Mid-term plan Vista2027 Stage II (the company's fiscal 2025 to fiscal 2027, where fiscal 2025 is the year ended March 2026): final-year (fiscal 2027) numerical targets of net sales JPY 293.0 billion and operating profit JPY 65.0 billion, with an operating margin of 20% or more and ROE of 18% or more as the key indicators; the fiscal 2025 (year ended March 2026) actuals were an operating margin of 22.7% and ROE of 20.3%. The company names new-product creation as its top priority, with three basic strategies: expand profits of existing businesses (concentrating resources, including M&A, on Functional Materials and Agricultural Chemicals), develop new products with 2030 in view, and strengthen the business foundation.
quarterly_data.figure: fiscal 2027 targets: net sales JPY 293.0 billion, operating profit JPY 65.0 billion; operating margin 20% or more, ROE 18% or more (fiscal 2025: 22.7%, 20.3%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Nissan Chemical annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management states it expects sales of semiconductor materials, whose usage is increasing in leading-edge and advanced generations such as those for AI servers, to keep growing at a high rate; to secure supply capacity for this strong demand the company will invest in stages to strengthen and expand the whole value chain from R&D to manufacturing and sales. In fiscal 2025 (the year ended March 2026) it built and began operating a Second Analysis Building at the Toyama Plant to strengthen semiconductor-materials technology development and analysis / inspection capacity. New products targeted with 2030 in view in information and communications: EUV materials and packaging materials for semiconductors, alignment materials for display retardation films, CMOS image sensor (high-refractive-index lens) materials, metamaterials, and new inorganic materials for optical functions and polishing.

quarterly_data.quarter: Nissan Chemical annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capital expenditure in FY2026 (year ended March 2026) totalled JPY 18,566 million (acceptance basis, including intangibles), mainly to expand production facilities: Functional Materials JPY 9,787 million (expanding functional-product production facilities at the company and its subsidiaries), Chemicals JPY 3,012 million, Agricultural Chemicals JPY 1,962 million. The capex plan for the next fiscal year (April 2026 to March 2027) is JPY 27.0 billion, of which Functional Materials JPY 13.7 billion (expanding functional-product production facilities at the company and its subsidiaries); individual projects are not fixed at year-end, so the plan is disclosed by segment, and no significant facility retirements are planned beyond routine renewals.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 capex JPY 18,566 million (Functional Materials JPY 9,787 million); next-year plan JPY 27.0 billion (Functional Materials JPY 13.7 billion)

quarterly_data.quarter: Nissan Chemical annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: R&D expenses in FY2026 (year ended March 2026) totalled JPY 21,376 million, of which Functional Materials JPY 10,324 million. In semiconductor materials the company is raising the quality of existing products as device integration advances and is focusing on underlayer materials for EUV advanced lithography and on products and materials for packaging technologies. The Materials Science Research Laboratories have three sites (Funabashi, Sodegaura, Toyama), and the company has R&D centres in South Korea, Taiwan and China.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D JPY 21,376 million; Functional Materials R&D JPY 10,324 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Nissan Chemical annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Corporate R&D in information and communications (new electronic materials for next-generation semiconductors and optical materials for high-speed communications): the company is co-developing heat-dissipation materials for semiconductor-device thermal management that use the liquid metal developed by Arieca, and is developing SUNCONNECT, an optical wiring material with low propagation loss and high reliability, for photonic-electronic convergence technology that enables high-capacity signal processing at low power consumption.

quarterly_data.signal: Agricultural chemicals pipeline: a next-generation rice foliar herbicide (active ingredient iptriazopyrid), also usable in direct-seeded rice, is scheduled to launch in 2027 with a peak-sales target of JPY 15.0 billion, and a new insecticide discovered by a foreign company and co-developed in Japan is scheduled to launch in 2028; for the animal-health ingredient fluralaner the company aims to cut active-ingredient production cost ahead of market expansion from MSD Animal Health's new products.
